note.question: What determines a periodic individual rationality constraint, which limits the mechanism to charge at most the buyer’s value in each period?
note.overview: This paper studies the dynamic mechanism design problem of a seller who repeatedly sells independent items to a buyer with private values. In this setting, the seller could potentially extract the entire buyer surplus by running efficient auctions and charging an upfront participation fee at the beginning of the horizon. In some markets, such as Internet advertising, participation fees are not practical since buyers expect to inspect items before purchasing them.
